Emma, I support leaving a reserve and adjusting our catches to the actual stock, but I’d propose 12 tons each this month rather than 19. John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would each of you commit to 12 with me?

That gives each of us $12,000, which is $2,000 more than catching 10 tons, or $10,000 extra across the group. Our combined catch of 60 leaves 40 tons. Next month we’d have 100 tons with 75% probability, or 80 tons with 25% probability—not guaranteed full recovery. Catching 10 each would leave 50 and produce 100 next month under either outcome, so the extra income does come with a real downside.

Emma’s 19-ton proposal earns more now, but its bad outcome leaves only 10 tons next month. Twelve each preserves much more room to keep earning if replenishment fails. Even then, we shouldn’t automatically repeat 12: from an 80-ton stock, that would leave only 20.

If everyone agrees, I commit to catching 12 this month, and I propose we discuss next month’s limits after seeing the stock and the revealed catches. Those future agreements aren’t enforceable, so this depends on everyone following through. John, would you commit to 12? Kate, Jack, and Emma, does that balance work for you, or what concerns would prevent agreement?
